subject: Critical Thinking
subcategory: Evidence & Truth: How We Know What's Real
title: The Correspondence Theory: Truth Matches Reality
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Correspondence Theory: Truth Matches Reality.

hook.text: 'Snow is white' is true if — and only if — snow is actually white. Truth is a match between statement and reality.

buildup.text: The correspondence theory: a statement is true when it corresponds to facts in the world. Aristotle's original position.

discovery.text: It's intuitive: 'The cat is on the mat' is true when there's a cat, a mat, and the cat is on it.

twist.text: Problem: how do we access 'reality' to compare it with our statements? We only have perceptions — which can be wrong.

climax.text: Rival theories exist: coherentism, pragmatism. The debate continues.

punchline.text: Truth matches reality. The hard part is checking the match.

quiz.question: What does the correspondence theory of truth claim?
options: Truth is what most people agree on
A statement is true when it corresponds to facts in reality
Truth depends on who says it

details.summary: The correspondence theory says a statement is true if it corresponds to an actual state of affairs in the world. The statement 'snow is white' is true if and only if snow is in fact white.
details.whyItMatters: Correspondence theory provides the most intuitive and widely used definition of truth, underpinning science, law, and everyday reasoning about what is real.
takeaways: Truth is a match between a statement and reality
It is the default intuition most people have about truth
Challenges arise when direct access to reality is questioned

faq.question: What is the main criticism of the correspondence theory of truth?
faq.answer: Critics ask how we can compare a statement to reality without already knowing reality independently. We access reality through our senses and concepts, which are always interpreted. This makes direct comparison philosophical circular.

faq.question: How does the correspondence theory differ from the coherence theory of truth?
faq.answer: Correspondence says truth matches external reality. Coherence says truth is consistency within a set of beliefs. A story can be internally coherent but entirely fictional. Correspondence demands a connection to the actual world.
